md_name: Pediatric Brain Tumor Radiotherapy Registry Workflow
md_description: This DAG represents a pediatric clinical registry for brain tumor radiotherapy, centered on patient cohort data, treatment parameters, modifications during therapy, and post-treatment side effects and interventions. It captures the clinical measurements and treatment course that support a dataset for studying how radiotherapy protocols influence tumor control and neurological outcomes in children.

pediatric_brain_tumor_patient_cohort.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic cohort identity and baseline biological/clinical properties of the enrolled pediatric patients, not any captured measurements, treatment parameters, outcomes, file-level details, or derived table fields. Because sample/subject identifiers are typically generated at the root Entity and should not be repeated elsewhere, I focused on cohort composition and stable patient attributes relevant to the registry’s clinical context. I excluded radiotherapy details, follow-up toxicities, and dataset assembly terms since those belong to downstream Capture/Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no explicit duplication constraints beyond the node-type boundaries.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the enrolled pediatric brain tumor cohort represented by this registry entry; use a stable string such as 'COHORT-001'. Assigned at enrollment/registry creation and used to link all downstream baseline, treatment, and outcome records.
Unique subject identifier for each pediatric patient in the cohort; use a stable string such as 'PT-0001'. Assigned at first registry inclusion and retained across all subsequent records.
Age of the patient at registry enrollment/baseline assessment, measured in years; typically pediatric range 0-18, recorded once at cohort entry.
Biological sex recorded from the medical record at enrollment for cohort description and stratification; use one of the allowed categorical values.
Patient height at baseline clinical characterization, measured in centimeters at or near registry enrollment; typically about 30-200 cm depending on age.
Patient weight at baseline clinical characterization, measured in kilograms at or near registry enrollment; typically about 2-100 kg in this pediatric cohort.

Primary brain tumor diagnosis used to define cohort membership, as documented in the clinical record at enrollment; examples include medulloblastoma, glioma, ependymoma, or other pediatric CNS tumor types.
High-level diagnostic grouping for the enrolled brain tumor used for cohort description and analysis; choose one category that best summarizes the primary tumor type.

Baseline disease stage, risk category, or clinical risk stratum assigned at enrollment, as recorded from the treating team; use the registry’s standard grouping terminology (for example, standard-risk, high-risk, metastatic, localized).

Brief baseline medical history relevant to registry characterization, recorded from chart abstraction at enrollment; include major prior conditions or notable neurologic history, not treatment events.
Whether the patient had a documented pre-existing neurologic condition before radiotherapy enrollment, captured from baseline history for cohort characterization.
Date the patient was entered into the registry cohort and baseline data collection began; format as YYYY-MM-DD.

baseline_clinical_data_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the baseline measurement session and the actively collected clinical intake variables that are recorded before radiotherapy: age, weight, and medical history. I excluded intrinsic cohort identity fields because those belong to the Entity node, and I excluded raw file/storage properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided treatment details, outcome/side-effect data, and any derivations. No already_generated list was provided, so I did not need to suppress duplicate field names from prior nodes beyond keeping the capture scope distinct from the cohort entity.

md_schema.descr: Date of the baseline clinical intake session when pre-radiotherapy data were abstracted for this patient; format YYYY-MM-DD and recorded at the time of registry enrollment or first pre-treatment assessment.
Age recorded during baseline clinical intake before radiotherapy, measured in years from the patient chart or intake form; typically pediatric range 0-18.
Weight recorded during baseline clinical intake before radiotherapy, measured in kilograms at the intake visit; typically about 2-100 kg depending on age.
Method used to obtain the baseline medical history during intake; indicates whether history was abstracted from chart review, caregiver interview, or both.
Baseline medical history text captured during pre-radiotherapy intake, including clinically relevant prior conditions and neurologic history as recorded by the registry abstractor.
Indicator of whether all planned baseline clinical intake fields were successfully captured for the patient at this session; used as a simple quality flag for the capture event.

baseline_registry_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data-artefact properties of the baseline registry records: file/storage format, record structure, size, and basic technical quality. I excluded the actual demographic and medical-history content because those are captured on the upstream Capture node and represented as cohort properties on the Entity node. I also excluded any treatment, follow-up, or computed fields since those belong downstream. No already_generated field list was provided, so I did not need to suppress overlaps beyond staying within the raw-artefact territory.

md_schema.descr: Technical file or record format of the raw baseline registry export containing demographic and medical history records; examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, or Parquet. Recorded for the signal artifact itself, not the clinical content.
Size of the raw baseline registry data file in bytes at the time it was archived or transferred; used to characterize the signal artifact and support reproducibility/transfer checks.

Number of raw patient-level records present in the baseline registry signal file; measured as the count of entries in the exported artifact, typically matching the enrolled cohort size or a subset if incomplete.
Number of columns/fields present in the raw baseline registry data structure at export time; used to describe the technical shape of the signal artifact.
SHA-256 checksum for the raw baseline registry file or object, recorded after export to verify integrity during storage or transfer; use a 64-character hexadecimal string.
Proportion of missing entries across the raw baseline registry artifact, calculated from the exported file to provide a technical completeness indicator for the signal; values range from 0.0 to 1.0.

radiotherapy_delivery_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the radiotherapy course was delivered: process timing, regimen/protocol parameters, operational adjustments made during therapy, and the responsible software/system identifiers if applicable. I excluded patient baseline properties, raw signal/file characteristics, and post-treatment outcomes because those belong to upstream Entity/Capture/Signal nodes or downstream Entity/Capture/Signal nodes. I also avoided fields that would describe the produced treatment records themselves, since those belong on the treatment signal node. No already_generated list was supplied, so I did not need to remove exact duplicates, but I kept the schema focused on process execution rather than cohort identity or output artifacts.

md_schema.descr: Date the radiotherapy delivery process began for the patient/course; format YYYY-MM-DD and recorded at the first delivered fraction or treatment initiation event.
Date the radiotherapy delivery process ended for the patient/course; format YYYY-MM-DD and recorded at the final delivered fraction or formal discontinuation.
Planned overall duration of the radiotherapy course in days, as specified before or at treatment start; typical values are positive integers reflecting the intended course length.
Categorical description of the planned dose delivery schedule used during the radiotherapy course; choose the standard scheme that best matches the protocol.
Whether any in-course treatment adjustments were made during delivery, such as dose changes, interruptions, replanning, or schedule shifts, as recorded by the radiation oncology team.
Type of in-course radiotherapy adjustment applied during delivery when a modification occurred; use one or more registry-standard categories if a change was made.

Total intended/actual delivered radiotherapy dose for the course, in Gray (Gy), as executed by the delivery process; typical pediatric brain tumor courses are often in the range of approximately 10-80 Gy.
Name of the treatment planning or record-and-verify software used to execute or manage the delivery process, if applicable; include the system name/version when available.
Version of the software or planning system used during the radiotherapy delivery process; record the exact release when available, such as 'v6.2.1'.
Overall operational quality indicator for the radiotherapy delivery process, summarizing whether the course was completed as planned or required notable deviations.

treated_patient_state.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only post-treatment patient status and intrinsic condition descriptors after radiotherapy exposure, not the treatment process itself, raw record properties, or the follow-up outcome measurements. Because the cohort and individual subject identifiers already belong on the root entity, I avoided repeating identifiers and focused on stable post-exposure clinical state relevant to describing the treated cohort. I also avoided any fields that would interpret or compute outcomes from follow-up data, since those belong to downstream capture/signal/derivative nodes. No already_generated list was provided, so there were no explicit name collisions to manage beyond respecting entity-level boundaries.

md_schema.descr: Stable subject identifier for the patient in the post-treatment state; use the same registry-linked string identifier carried forward from baseline, such as 'PT-0001'. Included here only when referencing the treated state record.
High-level clinical status of the patient after the radiotherapy course and any protocol modifications, as documented in the registry at the end of treatment or immediate post-treatment assessment.
Baseline-like description of neurologic condition after treatment exposure, reflecting the patient’s intrinsic state after the radiotherapy course rather than a follow-up outcome measurement.
Whether the patient required ongoing supportive care immediately after treatment completion because of the treated state; indicates presence of clinically meaningful post-exposure support needs.
Patient weight recorded after the radiotherapy course as part of describing the treated state; measured in kilograms near treatment completion and typically in a pediatric range.
Free-text summary of the patient’s condition after radiotherapy exposure, capturing clinically relevant observations about the treated state and any notable changes from baseline.

radiotherapy_treatment_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and actively recorded treatment variables from the delivered radiotherapy course: modality, dose, duration, fractionation, and any recorded modifications. I excluded baseline patient properties because those belong to the Entity/Capture upstream nodes, and I excluded raw file/storage details because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided any derived quality or analysis fields beyond simple capture completeness, since scientific interpretation belongs elsewhere. No already_generated list was supplied, so I focused on the capture-specific representation of the treatment course without repeating upstream cohort identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Date when the radiotherapy treatment details were abstracted or recorded from the delivered course; format YYYY-MM-DD and typically aligned with treatment completion or registry entry.
Radiation delivery modality recorded for the delivered course, such as photon-based external beam therapy or proton therapy; captured from the treatment record.

Dose prescribed or recorded for the delivered radiotherapy course, measured in Gray (Gy) at the treatment capture point; typical pediatric brain tumor values are often in the approximate range of 10-80 Gy.
Duration of the delivered radiotherapy course, measured in days from first to last fraction as recorded during treatment capture.
Number of fractions delivered or recorded for the radiotherapy course at capture time; typically a positive integer reflecting the treatment schedule.
Whether any treatment modifications were recorded for the delivered radiotherapy course during capture, such as interruption, replanning, or dose adjustment.
Free-text summary of any recorded modifications to the delivered radiotherapy course, captured from the treatment record and describing what changed during therapy.
Registry or clinical system from which the treatment details were captured, such as the oncology information system or registry abstraction interface; recorded to document the capture session source.
Indicator of whether all expected treatment fields were successfully captured for the delivered course; used as a simple completeness flag for the capture session.

treatment_details_signal.reasoning: I corrected the schema by removing field names that collide with previously generated DAG steps: file_format, file_size_bytes, record_count, and checksum_sha256. To stay within the Signal node’s territory, I replaced them with non-overlapping raw-artefact descriptors focused on the treatment-record signal’s technical structure and quality. I preserved the signal-level scope (artifact format, size, structure, integrity, completeness) but used distinct field names so the new schema does not repeat earlier metadata fields across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Technical file or record format of the raw radiotherapy treatment record artifact; examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, XML, or database extract. Recorded for the signal object itself rather than the treatment content.
Size of the raw treatment record artifact in bytes at the time it was exported or archived; used to characterize the signal file for storage and transfer.
Number of treatment records or patient-course entries present in the raw radiotherapy treatment signal; measured as the count of rows/objects in the exported artifact.
Number of data fields/columns included in the raw treatment record artifact; describes the technical structure of the signal export.
SHA-256 checksum for the raw treatment signal file or object, recorded to verify integrity after export or transfer; use a 64-character hexadecimal string.
Proportion of missing values across the raw treatment record artifact, computed from the exported file to provide a technical completeness indicator; values range from 0.0 to 1.0.

followup_outcome_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the post-treatment assessment session and the actively captured follow-up outcome variables: side effects, their severity/timing, and subsequent interventions required. I excluded baseline cohort attributes, radiotherapy delivery details, and raw file properties because those belong to Entity, Process, or Signal nodes respectively. I also avoided repeating any file-format or checksum-style identifiers previously flagged as collisions, and I used distinct field names for this node to stay within the follow-up capture territory. No other already_generated fields were provided in the prompt, so I kept the schema focused on the clinical outcome capture event.

md_schema.descr: Date of the post-treatment follow-up assessment when side effects and subsequent interventions were recorded; format YYYY-MM-DD and measured during routine or event-driven follow-up.
Time since radiotherapy completion at which the follow-up assessment was captured, measured in months; typically a nonnegative value indicating early or later post-treatment monitoring.
Whether any treatment-related side effects were documented during the follow-up assessment; captured directly from the post-treatment clinical evaluation.
Primary type of treatment-related side effect observed at follow-up; choose the category that best matches the documented toxicity or symptom.

Severity grade of the documented side effect, recorded at follow-up using the registry’s toxicity grading convention; higher values indicate more severe toxicity. Use the site-standard scale if available.
Number of days from radiotherapy completion to first documentation or onset of the follow-up side effect, when known; recorded as a nonnegative integer.
Whether any intervention was required after treatment because of the follow-up finding, such as medication, rehabilitation, hospitalization, imaging, or specialty referral.
Type of subsequent intervention required during follow-up after treatment-related side effects were assessed; use the category that best describes the action taken.
Free-text summary of the post-treatment follow-up assessment, including notable side effects and any subsequent interventions required, as recorded by the pediatric neuro-oncology follow-up team.
Indicator of whether all planned post-treatment follow-up outcome fields were successfully captured for this assessment session; used as a simple quality flag for the capture event.

toxicity_outcome_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw follow-up artifact properties for the toxicity/outcome records: technical format, size, structural counts, and integrity/completeness measures. I excluded the clinical toxicity content itself, because those side effects and interventions belong to the upstream follow-up Capture node, and I excluded treatment, cohort, and derived analysis fields because they are outside raw signal territory. I also avoided repeating any previously flagged file_format/file_size_bytes/record_count/checksum-style identifiers by using distinct signal-specific names for the artifact description.

md_schema.descr: Technical file or record format of the raw follow-up toxicity outcome artifact; examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, XML, or database extract. Recorded for the signal object itself rather than the clinical follow-up content.
Size of the raw follow-up toxicity outcome artifact in bytes at the time it was exported or archived; used to characterize the signal file for storage and transfer.
Number of follow-up records or patient-assessment entries present in the raw toxicity outcome signal; measured as the count of rows/objects in the exported artifact.
Number of data fields/columns included in the raw follow-up toxicity outcome artifact; describes the technical structure of the signal export.
SHA-256 checksum for the raw follow-up toxicity signal file or object, recorded to verify integrity after export or transfer; use a 64-character hexadecimal string.
Proportion of missing values across the raw follow-up artifact, computed from the exported file to provide a technical completeness indicator; values range from 0.0 to 1.0.

registry_table_assembly_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only table-assembly execution details, harmonization settings, merge strategy, and a process-level quality indicator. I removed the colliding software_version field flagged by the user and retained only non-duplicated process metadata. I excluded source-record content, raw file properties, and downstream table outputs because they belong to Signal or Derivative nodes, not the assembly process. The schema remains focused on how the analysis-ready registry table is produced from the three clinical streams.

md_schema.descr: Date when the registry table assembly process began; format YYYY-MM-DD and recorded when source clinical data streams were first merged/standardized.
Date when the registry table assembly process completed; format YYYY-MM-DD and recorded when the analysis-ready metadata table was finalized.
Number of source clinical data streams merged into the registry assembly process, typically including baseline, treatment, and follow-up signals.
Method used to harmonize and standardize source data during table assembly; select the primary approach used by the pipeline.
Primary strategy used during registry table assembly to handle missing values and incomplete records; captured as the process-level harmonization rule set.
Description of the key fields used to merge baseline, treatment, and outcome streams into a single registry table, such as patient_id and assessment_date; recorded at assembly time.
Name of the data management pipeline or software used to execute registry table assembly; include the exact system name used for the merge/standardization step.
Overall quality indicator for the registry table assembly process, summarizing whether the merged table was successfully standardized and ready for analysis.

analysis_ready_registry_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I kept only computed properties of the assembled analysis-ready registry table and avoided any upstream clinical content, process settings, or raw artifact metadata. I also corrected the prior collision issue by removing the duplicated column_count field and replacing it with distinct derivative-output descriptors. The remaining fields focus on table identity, versioning, row-scale, included variable scope, readiness, and quality, which are the minimum dataset-level details needed for downstream users to interpret the assembled registry output.

md_schema.descr: Name of the assembled analysis-ready registry table produced by the workflow; use a stable string such as 'pediatric_brain_tumor_radiotherapy_registry'.
Version identifier for the derived registry table, reflecting the release or rebuild iteration of the assembled dataset; use a stable string such as 'v1.0'.
Number of patient-course rows present in the analysis-ready registry table after assembly; counts the records available for downstream analysis.
Major categories of variables represented in the derived table, indicating whether baseline, treatment, and follow-up outcome fields are present for analysis.
Indicator that the derived table is suitable for downstream statistical analysis or machine learning use, based on the registry assembly outcome and QC checks.
Overall quality score for the assembled registry table, summarizing completeness and harmonization performance of the derivative output; use the registry’s internal scoring scale if available.
Number of distinct patient-treatment courses represented in the analysis-ready registry table; recorded as a dataset-level summary for the derivative output.
Whether the derived table includes follow-up outcome information relevant to tumor control and neurological outcomes for the cohort.
Total number of variables included in the assembled registry table after standardization; used as a derivative-level structural summary in place of the previously duplicated column count field.
